newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai stock accounts hit 10 mln for first time.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai stock accounts hit 10 mln for first time.

text.p: The number of trading accounts on the Shanghai stock exchange hit 10.02 million by Wednesday's close, surpassing 10 million for the first time, the Shanghai Securities News said on Thursday.
The newspaper said new accounts had increased quickly this year because of a surge in the domestic A share market, mainly due to an improvement in the national economy.
In May, the number of accounts exceeded eight million for the first time and in July exceeded nine million, it said.
"A fever to invest in the Shanghai bourse is spreading," the newspaper said.
New investors mainly come from areas outside Shanghai, such as Beijing, Guangdong, Jiangxi, Zhejiang and Hubei, it said.
China's A share markets have been on a bull run this year.

By Wednesday's close, Shanghai's composite index had risen by 88 percent to 1010.834 points from its close on the last trading day of 1995. Its Shenzhen counterpart rocketed 215 percent to 346.54 points over the same period.
Analysts say China's economy has entered its best period since 1993, with annual retail price inflation expected at below 7.0 percent this year, down from 14.8 percent in 1995.
